title: Impact of a Statewide Teleneonatology Acute Network in Bavaria (Tele-NNAD) on Patient- and System-Relevant Outcomes Compared with Standard Care: A Stepped-Wedge Cluster Trial Using a DOOR Endpoint and Win Ratio Analysis
summary:
Background
In many maternity hospitals, there is no on-site paediatric department. When complications occur in a newborn after birth, this can lead to delays in supply of specialized care. One possible solution is a real-time telemedical support from experienced paediatric specialists via secure video connection, making expert advice available at any time.
Research Question
This study aims to determine whether continuous access to remote telemedical support from experienced pediatric specialists in neonatology improves the care of newborns in maternity hospitals without own paediatric department compared to standard care without this support.
Methods
The study includes 19 maternity hospitals in Bavaria (spokes). At the beginning, all hospitals provide standard care without telemedical support. During the study, the new support system is introduced step by step according randomization across all participating hospitals. When a newborn presents medical problems, the maternity hospital can initiate immediately a video consultation with a specialized center (hub) and receives immediate expert consultation from a neonatologist.
The study lasts 12 months. During this time, important outcomes are compared, such as the health status of the newborn, whether transfer to another hospital is needed, and how quickly expert support is involved. The aim is to evaluate whether this new model of care leads to overall better outcomes.
conditions: Acute neonatal emergencies short before/after birth.

interventions.name: Arm 1 (Intervention): 24/7 acute teleneonatology support via a hub-and-spoke network (real-time video consultation with a perinatal center) in predefined neonatal emergencies (“trigger cases”). The intervention is applied on demand for each trigger case and is continuously available (24 hours/day, 7

Arm 2 (Control): standard care without structured teleneonatology support. Care is provided according to existing local standards. The control phase lasts until implementation of the intervention in the respective cluster.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Newborns delivered in one of the participating maternity units during the study period.
Presence of at least one predefined neonatal trigger criterion (acute clinical condition requiring neonatal decision support) immediately after birth.
Occurrence of at least one of the predefined trigger criteria from one of the 6 trigger groups A-F:
A: Perinatal risk: Emergency delivery, silent CTG, placental abruption, uncovered uterine rupture, suspected perinatal asphyxia
B: Resuscitation/severe primary adaptation disorder: Ongoing resuscitation (> 1 cycle of chest compressions), limp infant (> 5 initial ventilations with no response from the infant), umbilical cord pH <7.0 and/or BE < -16 mmol/l and/or 5-minute Apgar score < 6
C: Respiratory instability: Sustained oxygen requirement with CPAP support > 5 minutes
D: Other acute emergencies: Persistent cyanosis (> 5 minutes) of any cause
Severe recurrent hypoglycemia (<30 mg/dL), Suspected seizures
E: Severe malformations: MMC, abdominal wall defects, atresia, cleft lip and palate, and others
F: Prematurity <37 weeks of gestation: Prematurity <37 weeks of gestation
Exclusion criteria:
Newborns without any predefined trigger criterion.
Births outside the participating maternity units.
Newborns with missing or incomplete data required for the primary endpoint.
